learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of aws migration services and its relationship to Cloud Migration, Hybrid Cloud, and Specialized Infrastructure.
Interpret the example and identify at least one prerequisite or boundary relevant to aws migration services.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn aws migration services in the context of Cloud Migration, Hybrid Cloud, and Specialized Infrastructure. You will connect the listed subtopics to a practical decision, inspect a small example, and define evidence that would confirm or disprove your assumptions.
content.why_it_matters: AWS Migration Services matters because it is one part of migration, hybrid cloud and edge. Real workloads depend on explicit prerequisites, correct permissions, predictable behavior and a way to verify outcomes. Learning the decision points helps you distinguish a working demonstration from a safe and supportable design.

content_blocks.title: Module 22: Cloud Migration, Hybrid Cloud, and Specialized Infrastructure
content_blocks.alt_text: Five-step overview for module 22, Cloud Migration, Hybrid Cloud, and Specialized Infrastructure, followed by verification, least-privilege security, recovery, and cost-cleanup checks.
content_blocks.caption: Module 22 learning sequence: understand the concept, make a controlled design/configuration, verify behavior, and document security/reliability/cost trade-offs.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text:
**Core idea.** AWS Migration Services belongs to Cloud Migration, Hybrid Cloud, and Specialized Infrastructure. Migration and hybrid design begin with dependency discovery, security/data constraints, a workload-specific strategy, rehearsed cutover, observable validation and recovery planning.

The PDF lists these subtopics: AWS Application Discovery Service concepts; AWS Application Migration Service; AWS Database Migration Service (DMS); DataSync and Storage Gateway use cases. Treat them as a connected workflow rather than a list to memorize. Start with the workload requirement, identify the AWS resource/control involved, and write down who owns configuration and operation.

content_blocks.title: Practical reasoning
content_blocks.text: **Apply it safely.** For aws migration services, name the prerequisites and the expected result before making a change. Prefer a read-only inspection or local/static example first. Then plan a normal case, a failure case, and a verification step. In a live account, require the account owner-approved sandbox, narrow permissions, spend visibility and cleanup plan. Do not put credentials in code or commit local configuration files.

items.title: AWS Application Discovery Service concepts
items.text: Identify the AWS resource or design decision involved, the permissions and prerequisites it needs, and the evidence that shows it is configured as intended.

items.title: AWS Application Migration Service
items.text: Compare the available option with the workload requirement; record the operational, security, availability and cost trade-offs rather than assuming one option is always best.

items.title: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS)
items.text: Document the data shape, access pattern, retention, permissions, recovery path and performance needs. Verify query or storage behavior with representative synthetic data.

items.title: DataSync and Storage Gateway use cases
items.text: Trace the path from source to destination through address ranges, routing, gateways and filtering controls. Verify both forward and return paths; one successful configuration screen is not proof of reachability.

content_blocks.reset_steps: No AWS resource is created by this lesson example. If you independently run an approved lab, capture the starting state first, follow the lab-specific teardown instructions, check dependent resources and billing/resource inventories, and document anything retained.
content_blocks.limitations: The CodeLeaf playground is an HTML/CSS/JavaScript preview and does not execute AWS APIs, shell commands, SQL or cloud deployments. Treat output as illustrative; live values depend on credentials, permissions, Region, service state and schema.

content_blocks.title: Security and cost checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Use least privilege, keep Block Public Access/private defaults unless a justified reviewed requirement says otherwise, and document cost/cleanup before live changes.

task: Create a one-page decision card for “AWS Migration Services”. State the goal, prerequisites, the AWS resource or control involved, the expected result, one read-only/static verification step, one failure case, the relevant permission boundary, and cost/cleanup considerations. Do not create or alter billable resources unless the account owner has approved the lab.
hints: Start from the exact subtopics in the lesson and define the desired state in your own words.
Prefer a read-only check or static artifact before a mutating command; record the identity/Region and required permissions.
Verify the expected result and a failure path using current official documentation; write down cost and cleanup implications.
expected_output: A short reviewable decision card for AWS Migration Services with prerequisites, evidence, a failure case, security implications and cost/cleanup notes.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one successful example as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: The example may not test permissions, regional/service prerequisites, retries, recovery, quotas or edge cases.
common_mistakes.fix: Write acceptance criteria, test a failure path, inspect logs/state and record the limits of the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Changing a live resource before confirming its effect and cost.
common_mistakes.why: Cloud changes can expose data, break traffic or leave billable dependencies behind.
common_mistakes.fix: Start read-only, use an approved sandbox, review the change, tag ownership and verify cleanup.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying broad permissions or credentials into source files.
common_mistakes.why: Broad permissions and leaked long-lived credentials increase the impact of mistakes.
common_mistakes.fix: Use scoped roles/temporary credentials, keep secrets in approved stores and review access boundaries.

summary: AWS Migration Services is taught as part of Cloud Migration, Hybrid Cloud, and Specialized Infrastructure.
Migration and hybrid design begin with dependency discovery, security/data constraints, a workload-specific strategy, rehearsed cutover, observable validation and recovery planning.
Verify assumptions with official service documentation and evidence from the relevant AWS resource, logs or tests.
For live labs, confirm permissions and likely charges before acting, then verify cleanup.
